blocks.text: The reactivity of alkenes follows from the structure of the carbon-carbon double bond. This section describes the structure of ethene (11.7.1), the reactivity of the pi bond, carbocation stability and the inductive effect of alkyl groups (11.7.2) and the electron-withdrawing inductive effect (11.7.3). Alkenes are more reactive than alkanes, and their reactions mostly proceed through carbocations.
How does an alkane differ from an alkene in stability?
